summary: Step 3 (real AI providers + image gen + attachments) fully verified end-to-end. Backend pytest: 8/8 pass (streaming for chatgpt/gemini/claude returns real tokens, image gen produces real image served via /api/files, upload validates extensions and requires auth, perplexity provider rejected 400, guest can chat). Frontend playwright: login -> ChatGPT streams a real answer with typing cursor (not canned); multi-turn context works (follow-up 'which fruit did you just mention?' -> 'Pineapples.'); Gemini + Claude also produce real answers via model selector; Copy + Regenerate buttons visible on last assistant msg; model selector shows chatgpt/gemini/claude/image as Connected and quantum as Coming soon; Perplexity is NOT present anywhere in the UI/DOM; conversation persists across page reload; image mode indicator appears (purple), Nano Banana generated a real 1408px image which rendered via /api/files/quantum-ai/generated/...; attachment chips (note.txt + blue.png) shown in composer and in user message; ChatGPT correctly read the .txt content and returned 'BANANA-42'; uploading .exe triggers 'Unsupported file type.' toast; guest login on mobile 390x844 can chat with ChatGPT and gets real response 'OK'. No console errors beyond the expected 400 for the bad-extension upload test.
critical_code_review_comments: Regenerate button (Message.js) currently just re-sends the same user prompt (creating a new user+assistant pair) instead of replacing the last assistant message. Functionally acceptable, but produces duplicate user messages in history — consider replacing the trailing assistant message in place rather than appending a new turn.

server.py _build_image_contents silently swallows storage fetch errors (except pass). If an attachment image can't be fetched, the model won't see it but the user won't know — consider logging a warning and surfacing to client.
server.py /api/chat/stream persists messages only after the stream finishes; if the client disconnects mid-stream the partial assistant response is lost. Acceptable for MVP but worth noting.
ChatContext.sendMessage: `provider = model === 'image' ? 'chatgpt' : model` — safe fallback, but if user manually picks 'image' as model without imageMode toggle there's coupling to keep in mind.

server.py serve_file requires auth but does not check ownership (any authenticated user can fetch any /api/files/<path> if they know the exact opaque path). Paths are UUID-based so collision risk is low, but if strict access control is needed later, verify record.user_id == current_user.
